title: HEP seminar: Maria Artero Pons (Padova) – First Search for Sterile Neutrino Oscillation Leading to νμ Disappearance in the Booster Neutrino Beam at ICARUS
desc:
The ICARUS Collaboration successfully operated the 760-ton T600 detector at the LNGS underground laboratory before undergoing a major overhaul at CERN and relocating to Fermilab. Since 2021, ICARUS has been recording neutrino events from both the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) and the off-axis Neutrinos at the Main Injector (NuMI) beam. Now in its sixth year of continuous operation, ICARUS has demonstrated the maturity of large-scale Liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber (LAr-TPC) technology, providing a critical foundation for future experiments like DUNE.

In this seminar, the first search for muon-neutrino disappearance in the BNB using the ICARUS detector is presented. Neutrino events, identified as charged-current muon-neutrino interactions with a final state consisting of a muon and at…

title: SPC Seminar – Plasma – Charles Heaton (Imperial)
desc:
Title: Novel x-ray free electron laser based techniques for high-energy-density science

Speaker: Charles Heaton (Imperial)

Abstract: High energy density physics presents significant experimental and theoretical challenges, yet holds the promise of optimising inertial fusion energy experiments, a potential carbon-free power source. The advent of X-ray free-electron lasers has transformed the field, enabling unprecedented diagnostics and theoretical insights from groundbreaking measurements. This seminar presents two novel X-ray free electron laser based diagnostics for high energy density physics experiments: X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy and filtered X-ray diffraction. title: Spotlight on bacterial vaginosis: the hidden health crisis
desc:
New findings from the Imperial College London-led Spotlight on BV study reveal the hidden health crisis affecting 1 in 3 women.

One in three women will experience bacterial vaginosis (BV), yet most have never heard of it until it happens to them. Despite being the most common cause of vaginal discharge in the UK, BV remains overlooked, under-researched and widely misunderstood.

Join us for an exclusive lunchtime webinar presenting findings from the Imperial College London-led Spotlight on BV study , delivered in partnership with Brook Sexual Health .

Led by Dr Charlotte-Eve Short and Ms Sophie Stephens, this pioneering research shines a light on the real-world impact of a condition that affects millions but is rarely discussed openly.
